text: Rust rejects two simultaneous mutable references so one path cannot change a value while another still assumes it has exclusive, stable access. That rule stops data races and other memory-safety bugs caused by mutable aliasing, including iterator invalidation.
thought:
Rust forbids two mutable references to the same value to prevent data races. This prevents the bug class of concurrent modification.

The borrow checker enforces either multiple immutable references or exactly one mutable reference. This prevents aliasing bugs like iterator invalidation and use-after-free.
